tagline: Useful ingredients are hidden inside an ordinary seed.
profile: Botaneco develops ingredients from oilseeds for feed, food and personal-care products. problem: How do you separate useful components while retaining the properties a customer needs?
offering: Oilseed ingredients and a processing approach designed to preserve their functionality.
beneficiaries: Ingredient users developing aquaculture feeds, plant-based foods and personal-care products.
steps: A seed contains several kinds of material. Botaneco works with oilseeds including canola and sunflower.
The company describes an aqueous process for separating proteins and intact oleosomes while avoiding harsh processing conditions.

tagline: A chemical sample can produce a pattern we can interpret.
profile: Nanalysis develops and manufactures compact magnetic-resonance instruments and identifies its head office in Calgary. Its benchtop NMR products are used in areas including teaching, chemistry and food science. This example focuses on chemical analysis rather than medical imaging.

problem: How can an instrument reveal information that cannot be obtained by looking at a sample?

steps: Place a suitable sample in the instrument’s magnetic field. NMR concerns the magnetic behaviour of particular atomic nuclei.

tagline: A useful separation must work again and again.
profile: Summit Lithium Technologies, formerly operating as Summit Nanotech, develops direct lithium extraction technology. Its Calgary headquarters includes mechanical engineering, sorbent research and pilot-scale sorbent manufacturing. Its technology description combines a sorbent, a multi-column system and process modeling; other facilities and field activity are outside Canada.
local: Calgary headquarters, sorbent R&D, mechanical engineering and pilot-scale sorbent manufacturing. Commercial sorbent supply and field demonstrations are not assumed to be Calgary activities.
problem: How can a material repeatedly capture lithium from a mixture and then release it?
offering: Sorbent-based lithium-extraction systems and related process development.
beneficiaries: Lithium producers and resource developers evaluating brine-processing options.
steps: A brine contains lithium alongside other dissolved substances. Its composition affects how a separation must be designed.
Summit describes columns containing a sorbent that takes up lithium, followed by a step that releases lithium into another stream.
Columns operate through repeated stages. Testing considers not only one successful cycle but also performance as the material is reused.
Compare selectivity, recovery, water use and durability together. A result from one brine or test condition is not automatically transferable to every resource.
discussion: Would you choose a material that captures more lithium once, or one that performs consistently for many cycles?
activity: Give students fictional recovery values over five cycles for two sorbents. Ask which additional measurements would be needed before choosing one for a real process.
teacher_note: Use the data only as an illustrative comparison. Do not claim the exercise reveals Summit’s proprietary formulation or measured performance.

tagline: A digital view is useful only if it represents the place reliably.
profile: VEERUM is a Calgary-headquartered software company offering visual tools for industrial assets. Its published material describes bringing point clouds, 3D models and additional data together so users can inspect and discuss a site remotely. This story focuses on the relationship between a physical place and its digital representation.
local: Calgary headquarters and software-development business; customer assets may be elsewhere.
problem: How do you know a digital representation is accurate and current enough for a decision?
beneficiaries: Asset owners, engineering teams and people collaborating on industrial sites.
steps: A physical site can be captured in measurements and images, while design models describe intended structures.
VEERUM describes combining visual datasets, including point clouds and textured 3D models, with additional asset information.
To compare them meaningfully, users need compatible location references and an understanding of when the information was captured.
A detailed model may still omit an object, contain an alignment error or be out of date. The decision determines how much confidence is needed.
discussion: What would you check before using a digital model to decide whether new equipment will fit?
activity: Give students two fictional site drawings: one is precisely scaled but old, and one is recent but approximate. Ask which decisions each supports and what new measurement would resolve the gap.
teacher_note: Accuracy, completeness and freshness are different qualities. More realistic rendering does not guarantee a better measurement.

tagline: Storing energy changes when it can be used.
profile: Eguana Technologies lists Calgary as its headquarters and offers energy-storage systems and controls. Its products connect stored electrical energy with home and utility needs. A dated Calgary engineering posting also documents real work on power electronics, circuit boards and product testing.
local: Calgary headquarters and historical Calgary engineering evidence. Current manufacturing allocation is not inferred from older documents.
problem: How can energy storage help when electricity supply and demand occur at different times?
offering: Energy-storage systems and associated control technology.
beneficiaries: Households, installers and utilities managing energy availability and demand.
steps: Electricity demand and available generation can change at different times. A battery can store energy for later use.
Power electronics and controls manage electrical transfer between the storage system and other connected equipment.
A design must distinguish power, the rate of transfer, from energy, the amount stored or delivered over time.
Storage has losses and operating limits. Compare when energy is needed, how quickly it must be delivered and how much is available.
discussion: Could two batteries store the same amount of energy but support different appliances?
activity: Use fictional devices rated at 1 kW and 3 kW and an idealized 6 kWh store. Compare ideal run times, then ask what changes when losses and power limits are included.
teacher_note: Ideal answers are six hours and two hours, only if the device is within the system’s power limit. Real run time depends on usable capacity, operating conditions and losses; these are not Eguana specifications.

problem: How can an aircraft observation become useful information about the atmosphere?
offering: Aircraft communications, data systems and weather-sensing products.
beneficiaries: Aircraft operators and users of airborne weather information.
steps: An aircraft moves through changing atmospheric conditions, so a measurement needs a time, position and altitude to be meaningful.
The company describes weather observations from aircraft-mounted systems. The variables available depend on which system is used.
Communications and software move observations into tools for users. Reliability includes handling missing or delayed data.
Observations along flight routes can add evidence, but they do not sample every place equally. Coverage and instrument differences matter to interpretation.

activity: Give students a fictional route map with three aircraft tracks. Ask where observations would be concentrated and which regions would still need another source of measurement.
teacher_note: More observations are not the same as uniform coverage. Do not say all aircraft or all company systems measure humidity; the source distinguishes TAMDAR from AMDAR-over-AFIRS.
